newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.

text.p: * The upper Senate started emergency debates on a bank privatisation law, vital for the country's reform programme.
* President Emil Constantinescu met opposition leaders to discuss parliamentary support for the government's reform package.
Constantinescu said Romania was facing a difficult moment in its bid to apply tough reforms and that social unrest could be stirred by such measures.
* The ruling National Peasant Party backs a government decision to take control of the State Ownership Fund (FPS), the party's secretary general Radu Vasile said.
* Romanian Alternative Party expressed similar positions.
* Adrian Nastase, leader of the main opposition Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) said the party is against the government's plans to put the FPS under its control.

* Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea will meet the managers of state-run Petromidia refinery in the afternoon. Petromidia is one of two refineries on a government list of companies to be liquidated under a tough reform programme.
Petromidia managers want to persuade Ciorbea that the refinery does not have debts to the state budget and is still attractive for foreign investors. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
